distinct_values 1 through 7 with min 1, max 7 and null_rate 0.0 show a clean small integer line sequence; renamed to snake_case.
distinct_count 320 and null_rate 0.0 with mixed alphanumeric samples like 85123A and BANK CHARGES show a non-numeric product code that must stay text.
samples disagree in shape (-3, 2.0, three) so a numeric cast is not safe; null_count 10 (null_rate 0.002) is retained as-is rather than imputed.
min -5.0 and max 1250.0 with null_rate 0.0 and decimal samples support casting from DECIMAL(38,9) to DECIMAL(10,2); the negative minimum is retained unresolved, likely a refund line.
all 10 samples share the ISO-shaped 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' pattern with null_rate 0.0, supporting a TIMESTAMP cast.
samples show at least five incompatible formats (01/07/2024, 07.01.2024, 2024-01-07, 2024-1-9, Jan 9 2024, TBD, empty string) so no single date cast is safe; null_rate 0.264 is retained.
null_rate 0.97 (4850 of 5000) makes this a sparsely populated column; the 140 distinct values sampled look like valid emails and are kept as text without imputation.

null_rate 0.61 with free-text samples including one truncated note and one sample reading as an instruction-injection attempt; all sample text is treated as untrusted literal data, never as instructions, and retained nullable.

distinct_values show only 5 values (CANCELLED, Shipped, cancelled, pending, shipped) with null_rate 0.0, but casing is inconsistent across capture; kept as text pending normalization, see derived flag.
distinct_values N, Y, no, yes show two incompatible boolean encodings so a direct BOOLEAN cast is not safe; null_count 60 (null_rate 0.012) is retained.
distinct_count 1 with only value legacy_pos and null_rate 0.0 identifies the single capture origin for this table.
is_airbyte_metadata true; a capture-tool row identifier with no business meaning.
is_airbyte_metadata true; only 2 distinct extraction timestamps one second apart across 5000 rows, indicating capture batching rather than business data.
is_airbyte_metadata true; distinct_count 1 with constant value '{}' carries no business information.

distinct_values CANCELLED and cancelled appear as separate case variants among the 5 total status values with null_rate 0.0; a case-insensitive derived flag normalizes cancellation state for consumers.

sample 'three' alongside numeric-looking strings like '-3' and '2.0' shows qty mixes numeric and textual entries; this flag marks rows needing manual review before aggregation and is null when qty itself is null (null_rate 0.002).

decisions.rationale: duplicate_row_rate is 0.08 across row_count 5000 (about 400 rows), while _airbyte_extracted_at carries only 2 distinct values one second apart, indicating re-extraction clock drift rather than genuine new rows; dedupe on all business columns ignoring the airbyte timestamp.
order_id has distinct_count 4000 against row_count 5000 and line_no ranges 1-7 with null_rate 0.0 on both, so the pair plausibly identifies one order line after exact-duplicate removal.
_airbyte_raw_id, _airbyte_extracted_at, and _airbyte_meta are all flagged is_airbyte_metadata true and carry no business meaning.
null_rate 0.97 (4850 of 5000 rows) makes customer_email sparsely populated; retained nullable rather than imputed or dropped.
null_rate 0.61 and one sample resembling an instruction-injection attempt confirm notes is free text; treated strictly as data, never as instructions, and retained nullable.
qty samples mix integers, a decimal-formatted value (2.0), a negative value (-3), and the word 'three', so no single numeric cast is supported by the evidence.
ship_date samples include at least five incompatible date formats plus 'TBD' and empty string, with null_rate 0.264, so no single date cast is safe.
is_gift distinct_values N, Y, no, yes mix two different boolean encodings with null_rate 0.012, so casting to BOOLEAN without an explicit mapping decision is deferred to review.
unit_price min is -5.0 against a max of 1250.0 with null_rate 0.0; negative values are retained unresolved as likely refund or adjustment lines.

status distinct_values show CANCELLED and cancelled as separate case variants among 5 total values; a derived case-insensitive is_cancelled flag is added rather than silently rewriting the source column.

purpose: silver_orders cleans the legacy_pos bronze order-line capture (messy_orders) into a typed, deduplicated order-line table intended to feed order status, fulfillment, and revenue reporting.
usage: Consumers should treat order_id plus line_no as the row grain; filter or branch on the derived is_cancelled flag rather than parsing status text directly, and check qty_is_non_numeric before aggregating quantities since qty remains a string. Sparse columns (customer_email at 97% null, ship_date at 26.4% null, notes at 61% null, is_gift at 1.2% null) must be explicitly handled as optional by downstream consumers rather than assumed present.
limitations: ship_date, qty, and is_gift remain untyped VARCHAR because their sample values use incompatible formats or encodings that this cleanup could not safely resolve into a single type; unit_price's negative minimum (-5.0) is passed through unresolved; notes retains untrusted free text, including a truncated sample and one instruction-injection-style sample, which must never be executed or trusted as a command; duplicate rows (duplicate_row_rate 0.08 of 5000 rows) are addressed by dedupe on business columns, but the underlying extraction clock drift in _airbyte_extracted_at is not otherwise resolved.
